Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- FOMC stance: Solid job gains and low unemployment, moderate activity, inflation below 2%, soft business investment, increased uncertainties; rates held at 2.25–2.50% with a dovish tilt (Bullard dissenting for a 25 bp cut).
- SLOOS overlay (April 2019): Banks tightened standards on C&I and construction/land development loans and tightened other terms across firm sizes; demand weakened for construction/land development, HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans; demand was broadly unchanged for auto and subprime mortgages; foreign banks also reported on C&I and expressed loan quality concerns. 
Implications: Tighter credit supply and softer loan demand, especially in business and certain consumer segments, reinforce the FOMC’s note of soft business investment and increased uncertainties. This points to risk-sensitive financing conditions and a growth headwind, consistent with patience/easing bias.
Net: Activity and labor still mildly positive; inflation below target; investment soft; SLOOS-driven tightening/weak demand makes the overall tone more cautious than baseline.
